editorial:
You follow a TV reporter and her cameraman as they get trapped inside an apartment building that the CDC locks down after a mysterious virus starts turning people into bloodthirsty killers. Shot in a found-footage style, the movie puts you right in the middle of the chaos, making every hallway and dark room feel dangerous. The tension builds fast as the survivors realize they are stuck with infected residents and no way out. It is a tense ride that keeps you on edge from start to finish.

The acting feels natural and the pacing rarely slows down, which keeps the fear level high throughout. The camera work adds to the panic, though some viewers may find the shaky footage hard to watch. The story is simple but effective, and the scares come from real danger rather than cheap tricks. If you enjoy found-footage horror, this is a strong pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the reporter and cameraman reach the top floor and discover the source of the virus: a man who was trying to cure a rare disease but instead created the infection. They are attacked by infected people and the cameraman is killed. The reporter is dragged into the darkness by a creature, and the camera drops, ending the footage. The twist is that the virus was man-made, not natural, and no one survives to tell the story.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves found-footage horror and intense survival thrillers.
